thirtySeconds: KeithK75 won the net race at Shinnecock Hills at +1, eight shots clear of HamSammich at +9, with MashedBROtato another six back at +15. The raw scoreboard was even more decisive: Keith also took gross at -3, while Dan94 was the closest gross challenger at +19. Keith’s 17.79 strokes gained told the story, with 8.05 gained on approach, 6.68 around the green, 10 greens hit, four birdies, zero bogeys, and not a single three-putt. Behind him, the course turned into a group project nobody wanted: Ham finished +37 gross, DREADFUL lost 12.21 strokes, and Leroy found only one green.
latestTournamentTeaser: KeithK75 owned both the net race and the raw scoreboard, winning Shinnecock Hills at +1 net and -3 gross with 17.79 strokes gained. Behind him, the field produced four gross scores of +37 or worse, because apparently fairways and greens were considered optional.

carnage.name: Dan94
carnage.commentary: The opening drive found deep rough with 269 yards still to go, and the recovery only reached fairway. From there, seven more recorded swings were needed, including repeated fairway misses from seven yards and one yard out, before a 19-foot putt finally got close enough for a tap-in. A hole that began as a long second shot became a full-length documentary.

carnage.name: IUDoc92
carnage.commentary: The tee ball went to deep rough, the next one found sand, and the escape plan somehow became three more fairway attempts before the ball reached the green. A 25-footer was left a foot short, which was mercifully enough to end the expedition. Eight shots, zero sand saves, and a route map that looked like it needed a legend.

carnage.name: DREADFUL
carnage.commentary: The first shot missed into deep rough, the next reached fairway, and then the ball bounced between fairway and deep rough before finally reaching the green. An 11-footer was left one foot short and the tap-in closed out a seven-shot disaster. That was less a hole played than a prolonged negotiation with the simulator.

carnage.name: Leroy4522
carnage.commentary: The drive went to deep rough, the second shot found fairway, and the next two still left the ball short of the green. Then came a 32-footer, followed by putts from 41, 20, and 14 feet, with each one making the next look slightly less impossible. Eight shots and a tap-in later, the ball had traveled everywhere except efficiently.

carnage.name: HamSammich
carnage.commentary: The tee shot found deep rough, the second did it again, and the third was still 46 yards away in the same general neighborhood. Two more recovery attempts reached fairway territory before a six-foot putt finally ended the crawl. Seven shots for a net six: even the adjustment could only turn the wreckage into a slightly nicer wreckage.

carnage.name: KeithK75
carnage.commentary: The drive reached fairway, but the next shot finished 48 feet away before another swing sent the ball to deep rough. The next recorded shot was still in deep rough with 19 yards remaining, followed by a green-side recovery and an 11-footer that Keith actually made. The scorecard says seven; the shot log says the middle got weird, but the putter cleaned up the mess.

carnage.name: MashedBROtato
carnage.commentary: The tee ball missed into rough, the second shot only reached fairway, and the third finally got to the green with a 19-footer left. A 17-footer was pushed two feet short before the tap-in, producing a five-shot finish. Not catastrophic by this group’s standards, but still a par-three escape that required a small convoy.

players.name: KeithK75
players.tagline: Approach play so good it almost made the fairways look intentional
players.body: KeithK75 won the net tournament at +1 and the gross tournament at -3, finishing eight net shots ahead of HamSammich while also beating the raw field by 22 shots over Dan94. The numbers were ridiculous in the useful way: 17.79 total strokes gained, including 8.05 on approach, 6.68 in the short game, and 2.44 putting. He hit 10 greens, made four birdies, avoided every bogey and double bogey, and recorded zero three-putts on 24 putts. Even the worst hole ended with a made 11-footer after a trip through deep rough, while his notable card included two par-five birdies finished with tap-ins. Across seven prior starts, he had already averaged +3.86 net and +1.57 gross with two net wins and four gross wins; this was not a random heater. It was the strongest version of the KeithK75 problem, and Shinnecock got the full treatment.

players.name: HamSammich
players.tagline: A short-game survivalist trapped inside an approach-shot horror film
players.body: HamSammich took second net at +9 despite a +37 gross score, helped by a 28-shot net adjustment and a surprisingly useful 2.37 strokes gained putting. The raw golf was mostly a fight: four greens, seven bogeys, four doubles, and -2.06 on approach left him at -1.58 tee to green, though the total still landed slightly positive at 0.79 thanks to the putter. His worst hole required three straight trips into deep rough before four recovery swings and a six-footer finally ended the march, but he also made birdie on two par fives, including putts from 18 and 10 feet in the notable-hole list. With five prior starts showing an average +4.6 net but -2.19 total strokes gained, the second-place net finish is a real competitive result wrapped around another ugly gross card. The net game remains far more convincing than the raw one.

players.name: MashedBROtato
players.tagline: Bombs it 305 and then asks the ball where the green went
players.body: MashedBROtato finished third net at +15 and fourth gross at +39, with 4.79 total strokes gained led by 3.07 on approach and 0.92 around the green. The 317-yard longest drive and 305-yard average drive on fairways were loud, but three fairways and six greens were not exactly a matching set. He made three birdies, including a 25-foot bomb and two par-five birdies, yet eight bogeys and two doubles kept the scoreboard ugly. The worst hole was a five-shot escape after missing the green, reaching fairway on the second attempt, and leaving a 19-footer before two putts. His seven-start profile is mixed rather than clean: one net win, one gross win, and a near-neutral -0.06 average strokes gained, with the current +4.79 showing genuine raw improvement even if the card still came with plenty of loose change.

players.name: Dan94
players.tagline: Solid tee-to-green golf with one hole that needed its own zip code
players.body: Dan94 placed fourth net at +27 but was the gross runner-up at +19, an eight-shot gap created by the -8 net adjustment. The underlying round was respectable by this field’s Shinnecock standards: 6.79 total strokes gained, 5.71 tee to green, eight fairways, seven greens, and 31 putts without a three-putt. Then came the nine-shot crater: a drive into deep rough, a recovery to fairway, another fairway miss from 19 yards, more scrambling from seven and one yard, and finally a 20-footer before the tap-in. That single sequence explains why a player with solid approach and short-game numbers still finished nowhere near Keith. His seven-start history remains strong, with two gross wins, 11.97 average strokes gained, and a +4.29 average net, so this was more of a net-adjustment problem than a total collapse. The raw runner-up finish says the golf was there; the net board declined to care.

players.name: DREADFUL
players.tagline: The name matched the strokes gained, which is rarely a positive development
players.body: DREADFUL finished fifth net at +27 and sixth gross at +75, with a 48-shot net adjustment doing almost all the scoreboard heavy lifting. The raw numbers were savage: -12.21 total strokes gained, -6.09 off the tee, -4.34 putting, only three greens, 35 putts, three three-putts, four bogeys, and eight doubles. The worst hole began in deep rough, wandered through fairway and deep rough again, and ended only after a 12-footer was left one foot short. His seven-start profile was already firmly negative at -6.33 average strokes gained, with 5.71 greens and 33.86 putts per event; this round pushed every bad category louder. There were at least two net birdies in the notable-hole data, but they were buried under a gross card that looked like the course had started charging per mistake.

players.name: IUDoc92
players.tagline: One holed-out highlight surrounded by an ocean of recovery shots
players.body: IUDoc92 finished sixth net at +32 and fifth gross at +72, gaining 40 shots from the net adjustment but only -10.21 strokes gained from the golf itself. He hit two greens, made one birdie, putted 34 times, and lost strokes in every listed category, including -3.49 off the tee and -3.90 in the short game. The worst hole was a full wilderness tour: deep rough, sand, three more fairway attempts, then a 26-footer and a tap-in. There was one spectacular counterpunch, a hole-out from 18 yards for a net eagle, plus a made nine-footer elsewhere, but the rest of the card could not be bribed into cooperation. After seven prior starts with -9.32 average strokes gained and only 4.29 greens, this result confirms the profile more than it challenges it. The highlight reel exists; it is simply outnumbered.

players.name: Leroy4522
players.tagline: A putting marathon powered by one green and several bad ideas
players.body: Leroy4522 finished seventh net at +28 and seventh gross at +55, with -11.21 total strokes gained and only one green hit. He lost 3.55 off the tee, 2.04 on approach, 4.05 in the short game, and another 1.56 putting, while 36 putts and four three-putts turned every recovery into overtime. The worst hole started in deep rough, reached fairway, then required two more fairway recoveries before a 32-footer and three additional putts finally ended it. There were a couple of net birdie moments in the notable-hole list, including a made 11-footer, but they could not offset six bogeys and three doubles. His seven-start history already showed -5.74 average strokes gained, -4.36 approach, and 4.43 greens, so Shinnecock did not invent the problem; it simply gave it 18 more opportunities to introduce itself.

stateOfLeague: KeithK75’s seventh-start profile just got stronger: two net wins, four gross wins, and now a clean sweep at Shinnecock with +1 net and -3 gross. The event also sharpens the league’s central split: HamSammich and MashedBROtato remain legitimate net threats despite wildly ugly gross cards, while Dan94’s gross runner-up finish shows that raw golf and net positioning can still live in completely different zip codes.
